title: Block applies for federal bank charter to consolidate crypto custody
dek: Block Inc. applied to establish Builders Bank & Trust, an OCC-regulated national trust bank offering Bitcoin and stablecoin custody. The move would consolidate custody work currently run under more than 50 state money transmitter licenses into a single federal charter.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Block's application targets consolidation of custody operations across 50+ state licenses under one OCC-regulated federal trust bank.
bottom_line: The OCC review timeline for Builders Bank & Trust will set expectations for when Block can begin consolidating its state licenses. Watch whether approval arrives before or after other major custody platforms seek similar federal charters, as the order of entry may shape how the regulator structures oversight of blockchain-native banking infrastructure.
body: Block Inc. applied to establish Builders Bank & Trust, an OCC-regulated national trust bank that would offer Bitcoin and stablecoin custody services, according to reporting from September 8, 2026.

The application marks a structural shift in how Block manages its custody operations. The company currently runs custody work across more than 50 state money transmitter licenses, per The Defiant's reporting. A federal charter would consolidate those operations under a single regulatory framework administered by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

Builders Bank & Trust would operate as a trust bank under OCC supervision, handling Bitcoin and stablecoin custody as core services. The move reflects broader industry adoption of federal banking infrastructure as a path to streamline regulatory compliance and reduce the operational burden of maintaining licenses across multiple jurisdictions.

The application arrives amid other major infrastructure players exploring similar paths toward federal banking charters. The OCC has signaled openness to chartering banks that offer digital asset services, though the approval timeline and specific regulatory requirements for Builders Bank & Trust remain unaddressed in available reporting.
